results.title: Layered Bus Crossbar
results.prompt: Draw a directed artificial crossbar graph with three horizontal buses. The top bus has nodes T0,T1,T2,T3,T4, the middle bus has M0,M1,M2,M3,M4, and the bottom bus has B0,B1,B2,B3,B4. Add directed bus edges Ti->T(i+1), Mi->M(i+1), and Bi->B(i+1) for i=0..3. Add vertical relay edges T0->M0->B0, T2->M2->B2, and T4->M4->B4. Add crisscross transfer edges T0->M2, T1->M3, T2->M4, M0->B2, M1->B3, M2->B4, plus feedback edges B1->M0, B3->M2, and M4->T3 routed outside the buses. Add source S connected to T0,M0,B0 and sink R reached from T4,M4,B4. Keep the buses aligned and compact while routing transfers clearly.

suggestions: Place T0-T4, M0-M4, and B0-B4 on three straight horizontal rows with consistent column spacing, especially aligning relay columns 0, 2, and 4 vertically.
Move M2 back onto the middle bus row and move B1 and B3 up onto the bottom bus row to restore the crossbar grid.
Route crisscross transfer edges with shallow bends or separated diagonal corridors so they do not cluster around M2/M3/M4.
Reroute M4->T3 outside the buses with a shorter upper or right-side loop that stays farther from T4->R and T4->M4.
Keep S just to the left of the three row starts and R just to the right of the three row ends, with short direct fan-in/fan-out edges.

visual_issues: The three buses are not drawn as clean horizontal rows: T3 is raised above the top bus, M2 is raised above the middle bus, and the bottom row is uneven with B1/B2 lower than B0/B3/B4.
The bottom bus is overly stretched, especially the large gaps from B2 to B3 and B3 to B4, creating long bus edges and a less compact drawing.
Several transfer and feedback edges form a visually tangled central region around M0, M1, M2, B1, and B2.
The diagonal edge from M1 to B3 passes through the central lower area close to B2 and contributes to ambiguity with nearby edges.
The feedback routing from B1 to M0 runs very close and nearly parallel to the M0-to-B2 edge for a noticeable segment, making direction and edge identity harder to read.
The outside feedback edge M4 to T3 is not clearly routed outside the buses; it cuts diagonally through the upper-right transfer region.

Use consistent column alignment for relay columns T0/M0/B0, T2/M2/B2, and T4/M4/B4 to make the crossbar structure easier to read.
